study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Kim et al., Biological Psychiatry: Global Open Science, 2025
study_identification_part.si4_title: Predicting Mental and Neurological Illnesses Based on Cerebellar Normative Features

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract and methods clearly state the objective: to test the predictive value of individual deviations from cerebellar normative development for several disorders (ASD, BD, SZ, MCI, AD). The purpose of applying normative modeling is explicitly for prediction/classification using deviation-based features (median, variance, percentage of extreme deviations) across multiple atlases.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "Here, we used machine learning to test the value of individual deviations from normative cerebellar development across the lifespan ... for prediction of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) ... bipolar disorder (BD), schizophrenia (SZ), mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and Alzheimer’s disease (AD). We applied several atlases and derived median, variance, and percentages of extreme deviations within each region of interest."; "Our study highlights the utility of cerebellar normative modeling in predicting ASD and SZ"

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: An EXISTING cerebellar normative model is used and the original publication is cited. QC and exclusion procedures are described (ACAPULCO QC; exclusion of outliers; sites with <5 participants). Final sample sizes for training and test sets of the reference (neurotypical) cohort are reported (n=27,117 train; n=26,985 test). However, detailed inclusion/exclusion eligibility criteria for the healthy reference cohort are deferred to the cited work and are not fully specified here.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "The study sample consisted of individuals from the cerebellar lifespan normative model (15), where individuals without a diagnosis were split into a training set (n = 27,117), a test set (n = 26,985), and a clinical set (n = 1757)."; "We performed quality control ... running the ENIGMA Cerebellum Volumetric Pipeline QC Scripts of ACAPULCO ... Approximately 5% of scans were inspected manually ... We further excluded participants whose scans revealed outliers in at least two regions, as well as when a scanning site contributed data from fewer than five participants."; "Full Sample description and demographics ... Training set 27,117; Testing set 26,985"

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing software and steps are described for lobular and voxel-level pipelines (FreeSurfer 5.3 skull stripping; FSL reorientation and FLIRT registration; intensity normalization; ACAPULCO segmentation with N4 bias correction and ANTs registration; SUIT VBM). Quality control procedures are also described in the Supplementary Methods.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "The T1-weighted images were skull stripped using the FreeSurfer version 5.3 ... reoriented to the standard FSL orientation ... Linear registration was performed using FLIRT ... voxel intensity values ... normalized to (0, 1)."; "To segment the cerebellum, we utilized ... ACAPULCO ... images were corrected for inhomogeneity by the N4 correction method and registered to the 1-mm isotropic ICBM 2009c template using ANTs."; "We used SUIT ... to segment cerebellar gray and white matter voxel-based morphometry maps."; "We performed quality control ... ENIGMA Cerebellum Volumetric Pipeline QC Scripts of ACAPULCO ... excluded participants with outliers ..."

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: Deviation scores are conceptually described and used to compute features (median, variance, percentage of extreme deviations). The paper explains that deviations represent departures from typical ranges. However, explicit quantitative thresholds (e.g., |Z| > 1.96) and detailed interpretive guidance on direction/magnitude are not reported.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: "The deviation refers to instances where an individual falls outside the typical range."; "We applied lobular and voxelwise normative models ... and aggregated the median, variance, and percentage of extreme deviations across atlases."
